I am a Finnish woman and I think while in Korea I never met a "normally interacting man".. I am talking about people I met not searching to have any relationship with, but just people I met kind of "naturally". They all came on to me very strong, being kind of demanding and having expectations on how I should act or behave while at the same time not being able to hold a REAL conversation. I mean to really talk about serious issues and share their thoughts, so everything always felt shallow and not leading to any understanding between me and these people. Like this one man (my worst experience) to whom I made very clear for many times straight from the beginning that I was not interested in any other kind of relationship with him, but meeting (around a cup of coffee/tea) as acquaintances sometimes could be ok.. He started to buy me all kinds of gifts, clothes etc. and no matter how strictly I said "NO" and "PLEASE DO NOT BUY ME ANYTHING" etc. he did not listen. He sometimes got mad when I asked him to take those gifts back (he knew where I lived so he brought the stuff to my door..), but still did not stop. Then he even bought a ring wanting me to marry him. And I was like WTF is this.. Not once when we met did we have any kind of a real conversation. He was basicly able to talk about his work and maybe the weather but nothing real.. I come from a culture where when we talk, we talk about real stuff, even small talk is considered waste of time and also NO is considered NO and usually ONE time saying NO is enough. (Unless the other person is some kind of a psychopath.) So I always felt like I was not able to connect with these Korean men at all. The men I met were all around the 40's and older cause I am older too and I wonder if the younger generations act differently, but for me I had zero good experiences with the Korean men I met. And this man I talked about, in the end I had to go back to Finland to be able to disappear and cut ties with him. Cause the word NO really meant nothing to him. After 9 months I went back to Korea and luckily never saw him again. (This happened 3 years ago.) Anyway, I am sure there are many good men in Korea - like Megan's husband - but I just never met any of them.
